opening.argument: The presentation is framed as a discussion of cryptocurrency and future development, not as a request to transfer money or provide credentials. The speaker describes building a system where users can bring any wallet, transact with any asset, and operate across chains, while also addressing self-custody, privacy, and reliable user interfaces. The ShapeShift functionality and transfer-fee example therefore appear as parts of a product and technology presentation rather than a standalone financial solicitation. The discussion remains exploratory, with the speaker acknowledging that he does not have all the answers and describing a future-oriented goal. It also recognizes limitations and risks, including the possibility of permanently losing access after losing a recovery phrase, which supports an educational context rather than an unqualified financial promise.

citations.quote: And here today, I'm going to talk to you about crypto.
We're trying to solve this issue where you can bring any wallet you want come in and transact with any asset you want on any chain.
I don't have the answers and I hope that there are builders in the audience that think of the answers that make this future reality.
We have to be reliable when a user clicks a button on a UI.
I hope that we can build into a better Multi chain self-custodial future.
